decision_record.calculation: Fixture: C1 fire (price 4.00, ret60 40, vol20 0.10, adv $3M, atr_ratio per book) dated 2026-10-19 vs session 2026-10-26 (age 7d): control enters 100 shares ($400 ticket), treatment refuses with paired record age_days=7; fire dated the session date enters identically under both. BETA fire (price 50, m2_qualified) age 7d: control enters 8 shares, treatment refuses.
decision_record.comparison: Baseline (after batch-12 repricing): a fire dated any number of sessions before the current session still deploys the $400 ticket at the current price. Comparator: identical fire/bars; fires with age outside [0, 1] sessions (the delay mode's own constant) refused, future-dated refused.
decision_record.experiment: tests/test_harden_edge_batch11_blockers.py TestTensorFireAge: stale refused + journal record for all four sleeves, fresh enters, switch OFF restores any-age entry exactly. Rejection rule: refusal of a fire aged 0-1 sessions, or entry on a fire aged >1 session with the switch ON.
decision_record.mechanism: Responsiveness/perception (unbounded signal age): the tensor producer's freshness SLA (86400s) bounds the bundle FILE, not the fire's date inside it; a stale bundle or a backlog fire passes every gate and buys days after the signal died.
decision_record.transfer: A Tensor fire is a perishable signal (buy-cyan / M2 cohort qualification at a point in time); its surplus decays with age. The sleeve's own design acknowledges this — delay/reserve modes wait exactly one session — yet cash mode placed no bound on fire age at all.

disposition: ENHANCED: fire-age bound (<=1 session) on cash Tensor entries (second look after batch-12 repricing)
